neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was married to the deceased, was alleged to have subjected her to cruelty and harassment due to dowry demands. The deceased's father and brother provided statements to the police, claiming that the accused and his family demanded dowry and that the deceased was harassed. The deceased sent several letters to her father and brother-in-law, expressing her grievances about the treatment by her in-laws. The deceased died in a hospital, and the police lodged an FIR against the accused and his family. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 304-B IPC, but the High Court acquitted the mother-in-law and reduced the sentence of the accused. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction, finding that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of the offence, including the demand for dowry and the proximity of the harassment to the deceased's death.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution relied on the statements of PW3 (father of the deceased) and PW4 (brother of the deceased), as well as letters written by the deceased, to establish that she was subjected to cruelty relating to dowry demands soon before her death. However, the court found these statements and letters insufficient to prove the necessary elements of the offense under Section 304-B IPC.

quotes.text: The prosecution relied upon the statement of PW3-father and PW4-brother of the deceased which has been made basis of conviction by courts below.

defence_argument.value: The defense argued that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of Section 304-B IPC, specifically that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment related to dowry demands soon before her death. The defense emphasized the lack of independent evidence and the absence of proof regarding the timing of the alleged harassment.

quotes.text: The prosecution has failed to prove the essential ingredients of Section 304-B IPC.

defence_argument.note: no quote occurs in the judgment; closest passage (p.2, match 72): "596-A-C] 1.2 The prosecution has failed to prove either the demand of dowry or that any such demand was raised soon before h er"

legal_principle_applied.value: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish a proximate nexus between the deceased's death and the cruelty or harassment inflicted on her due to dowry demands, and that the term 'soon before her death' implies a close temporal relationship between the harassment and the death.

quotes.text: There must be material to show that soon before her death the victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment.
